headline: HSBC launches HKD stablecoin RedCoin as Bitcoin steadies above $81K and PEPE surges 10%
summary: The day's biggest story came from traditional finance: HSBC rolled out RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, to more than 3 million retail customers — the most significant bank-issued stablecoin launch to date. Bitcoin held relatively steady, dipping less than half a percent to around $81,500 as the prior session's AI-sector selloff faded. Altcoins staged a partial recovery, with meme coins leading the way; PEPE jumped nearly 10% while most large-caps posted small losses.

winners.name: Pepe
winners.catalyst: PEPE surged as risk appetite returned to the lower-cap speculative segment of the market following the prior day's equity-driven selloff, with Bitcoin stabilizing above $81,000 giving traders confidence to reach for higher-risk assets.

losers.name: Quant
losers.catalyst: No specific catalyst was identified for Quant's decline; the drop likely reflects continued altcoin weakness and residual pressure from the tech stock selloff spilling into crypto.

whyItMoved:
The session was shaped by two forces pulling in opposite directions. On the macro side, the previous day's sharp selloff in AI and tech stocks — which had dragged crypto lower alongside equities — began to fade, removing the immediate pressure on Bitcoin. BTC found its footing above $81,000 and barely moved, ending the day down 0.45%. That stabilization was enough to bring risk appetite back to the smaller end of the market: meme coins and lower-cap altcoins attracted fresh capital as traders who had pulled back during the equity rout returned. PEPE was the clearest beneficiary, climbing nearly 10% as speculative interest concentrated in assets that had sold off hardest the day before.

The broader top-15 picture was mostly red but quietly so. Ethereum slipped 0.34%, Solana fell 0.57%, and XRP dropped 0.89% — none of these moves suggest a new leg lower, just residual softness. Monero was the notable exception among large tracked assets, falling 5.74%, though no specific news drove that move. Zcash also dropped 3.39%. BNB bucked the trend with a 1.53% gain, the strongest performance among the top-10 assets.

The Fear & Greed index sits at exactly 50 — neutral — which matches the day's tone: not a recovery, not a continuation of the selloff, just a market catching its breath. The bigger story today was not price action at all but HSBC's RedCoin launch, which represents the most significant entry by a global bank into the retail stablecoin market.
worthKnowing: HSBC launched RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, to more than 3 million retail customers — the first retail stablecoin issued by a major global bank.

Ethereum developers postponed a testnet deployment of the Glamsterdam upgrade after security researchers flagged potential risks to existing smart contracts, adding uncertainty to ETH's near-term development timeline.
South Korea is moving to amend its foreign exchange law to regulate stablecoins as payment instruments, a significant policy shift in one of crypto's largest retail markets.
Crypto custody firm Fireblocks denied a report that Visa was in acquisition talks to buy it for approximately $2.5 billion.
